ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two common nodes on the left and right, and the middle branch is resistor R, directly connected between these two nodes. The upper branch and lower branch each have an identical battery, both labeled E, r, and with the same polarity: positive terminal on the left and negative terminal on the right. Therefore two identical batteries with internal resistance and resistor R are connected in parallel across the same pair of nodes. Reasoning: Each battery can be regarded as a non-ideal source with electromotive force E in series with internal resistance r. When two completely identical non-ideal sources with the same polarity are connected in parallel, their equivalent Thevenin electromotive force is still E, and the equivalent internal resistance is r in parallel with r, namely r/2. Thus resistor R is powered by the equivalent source E and series internal resistance r/2, so the current through R is I = E/(R + r/2) = 2E/(2R + r).

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the upper and lower battery branches are identical and connected across the same two nodes as R, with the same polarity. Let the current supplied by each battery branch be i. By symmetry the two battery currents are equal, and by KCL the resistor current is I = 2i. The voltage across R is IR. For each nonideal battery branch, the terminal voltage across the same two nodes is E - i r. Equate the common node voltage: IR = E - i r.
